_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel finally broke — down to $4.57/gal, off nearly 80 cents from June. That's real margin back in your pocket, so don't hand it to the broker as a rate cut. Trade reports again say dry van spot is running above contract and flatbed's at record highs — hold your ask, especially reefer out of Georgia produce lanes. Spot $/mi numbers below are still last cycle's; couldn't get a clean primary-source read on today's exact rate this week.

_sourcing.status: diesel promoted to live (WebSearch-corroborated, EIA-cited); everything else carried-forward. See refreshBlockers.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE (partial): $4.57/gal (also reported as $4.578), week ending 2026-07-06, per EIA weekly on-highway diesel report as cited by two independent WebSearch queries returning matching precise figures and a coherent declining trend ($5.35 on 6/1 -> ~$4.67 on 6/22, flagged last cycle -> $4.578 on 7/6). Direct WebFetch to eia.gov (petroleum/gasdiesel, dnav tables) still returned HTTP 403 both attempts today, so this is search-engine-mediated, NOT a primary-source fetch. Confidence: medium-high (internally consistent across 2 queries + prior week's flagged number), not certain.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 snapshot. Not verified this cycle — could not confirm against a primary source (DAT trendlines WebFetch blocked, 403).
_sourcing.modality: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 modality ranges. Not verified this cycle. Trade-press signal this week (DAT-cited via WebSearch) says dry van spot has moved above contract and flatbed hit a record high, and reefer linehaul is strong out of Georgia produce lanes — directionally consistent with the existing 'up' trend, but the WebSearch snippets gave internally inconsistent numbers for the same metric in the same response (e.g. reefer linehaul quoted as both $2.68 and $2.74/mi, flatbed as both $3.69 and $2.99/mi within one query) so nothing numeric was promoted.
_sourcing.commodityRates: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle. WebSearch flagged Georgia (tomatoes/watermelons) as the new Southeast reefer hot spot as Florida's produce season closes, and a Laredo->Boston spike — real signal, not promoted to the lanes list without a verifiable rate.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle to lead with the live diesel number; rate-stance coaching is carried-forward, reinforced by (unverified) trade-press directional signal.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Multiple trade-press/DAT-blog headlines (via WebSearch, not primary-fetched) again suggest dry van spot is running above contract for the first time since Feb 2022, flatbed is at a record high, and Southeast reefer is tight (Florida season closing, Georgia opening at higher rates). Same signal flagged last cycle, still not verified against a primary source — do not put into the numeric fields until WebFetch to dat.com/trendlines succeeds.

refreshBlockers: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for every external host tried this session (eia.gov x2, dat.com/trendlines, indexbox.io, fred.stlouisfed.org, en.wikipedia.org as control) — same org egress-policy block via the agent proxy as the 07-07 attempt, confirmed still active (proxy status shows enabled:true, no relay failures logged — it's a destination-side 403, not a proxy outage). WebSearch itself works and this cycle gave internally CONSISTENT results for diesel (2 independent queries, matching $4.57/$4.578 figures, coherent trend) so that field was promoted to live; spot/modality numbers were again internally inconsistent within single WebSearch responses (contradictory reefer/flatbed figures in the same answer) so they were NOT promoted. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) would let this go fully live.
